greet: Hi, I am Tilly. Let us learn this together.
Hello. {steps} short steps, and I will be right here.
finish: Track done. Take a bow.
Every step, done. I am proud of you.
That is the whole track. Come back for another when you like.

agentDone: The agent finished. You approved it from right here.
Done, and you never lost your place.
agentWorking: Your agent is working. You are free to wander.
close: Closed, and the rest made room.
Tidy. One less window to think about.
command: Nice. That ran just like on your machine.
copy: Copy mode, like vim. Your hands already know it.
Found it. Search works in any pane.
explainer: Worth trying once tuios is on your machine.
That one needs a real machine. Now you know where to look.
float: Floating. It sits above the tiles now.
focus: Nice hop. Watch the bright border follow you.
Focus moved. You are over there now.
help: Help is always one key away.
Now you know where the answers live.
menu: The menu shows what each key does.
That menu is there whenever you forget a key.
move: That window found a new spot.
open: New window. Every session starts like that.
There it is. A shell of your own.
palette: The palette finds any action by name.
Type what you want, press enter. That is the palette.
resize: A little bigger here, a little smaller there.
rotate: Rotated. The split turned on its side.
A quarter turn for the layout.
screensaver: Nice screen saver. I like that one.
scrollback: Your whole history, one key away.
send: Sent to workspace {n}, and you followed it.
Packed up and moved to workspace {n}.
settings: Settings live here. Nothing to edit by hand.
That is where the knobs are.
showkeys: Showkeys is on. Handy when you share your screen.
Now everyone watching can see your keys.
sidebar: The rail shows every session at a glance.
There is the rail. Everything in one list.
skipped: Skipped. You can come back to it any time.
No problem. On to the next one.
split: Clean split. Two panes, one screen.
Split. My face works the same way.
switcher: The switcher. Pick a desk, any desk.
tape: The tape played itself. That was tuios driving.
All scripted. You just watched a tape.
tiling: Tiling does the arranging for you.
typing: Typing mode. Your keys go to the shell now.
Green badge. The shell is listening.
windowMode: Back in window mode. Keys move windows again.
Window mode. Your keys drive tuios.
workspace: Workspace {n}. Your other windows are safe where you left them.
yank: Yanked. It is on your clipboard.
zoom: Zoom in, zoom out. Handy for a closer look.
Zoom is the quickest way to focus on one thing.

altBlocked: Your Option chords are not reaching tuios. Something outside the browser may be taking them. The note on the card explains.
idle: Take your time. The hint on the card has the next key.
No rush. The glowing key is the one to press.
Still with you. Click the terminal first if keys do nothing.
noWindow: There is no window to work with. Press n for a new one.
showMe: Want a demo? Show me does it slowly, then it is your turn.
Stuck is fine. Show me will play the keys for you.
wrongKeys: Close. Check the order of the keys on the card.
Not that one. The hint on the card will help.
wrongModeTerminal: You are in window mode. Press i to type into the shell.
wrongModeWindow: You are typing into the shell. ctrl+b, then esc, gets you to window mode.

poke: My eyes are two panes and my mouth is a prompt.
Show me is there any time you want a demo.
Three esc presses take you out of the terminal.

tracks.title: The basics
tracks.blurb: Windows, typing, the leader key and help. From zero.

greet: Hi, I am Tilly. We start from zero, one key at a time.
Hello. I live in a terminal too. Let us open your first window.
finish: That is the basics. You can drive tuios now.
Windows, modes, the leader key and help. All yours.

steps.title: Open a window
steps.note: You start in window mode. Keys move windows.
steps.hint: Press n. You start in window mode, where n opens a window.

web.hint: Click the dark area first, then press n.

steps.title: Start typing in it
steps.note: i flips to typing mode. Watch the badge.
steps.hint: Press i. The badge turns green and says TYPING.

steps.title: Say hi to the shell
steps.note: Your keys go to the program now.
steps.hint: Type fastfetch and press enter.

steps.title: Split with the leader key
steps.note: ctrl+b, let go, then a key. It works in any mode.
steps.hint: Hold ctrl, tap b, let go. A menu pops up. Now press |.

steps.title: Back to window mode
steps.note: ctrl+b, then esc. The badge flips back.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, let go, then esc.

steps.title: Hop between windows
steps.note: The bright border follows you.
steps.hint: In window mode, tab moves to the next window.

steps.title: Close one
steps.note: No prompt, no fuss.
steps.hint: In window mode, x closes the window with the bright border.

steps.title: Every key, one page
steps.note: Forgot a key? It is in here.
steps.hint: Press ? to open help. Look around, then esc to close it.

steps.title: Or just search for it
steps.note: The command palette runs anything by name.
steps.hint: ctrl+p opens the palette. Type zoom and press enter.

tracks.title: Coming from tmux
tracks.blurb: Turn on the tmux keys. Your fingers already know the rest.

greet: Coming from tmux? First we turn on your own keys.
Hi. ctrl+b leads here too, and the tmux preset does the rest.
finish: Done. Your tmux keys work here, and window mode is a bonus.

steps.title: Pick the tmux keys
steps.note: U opens the keybind presets. tmux is the second row.
steps.hint: Press shift+u. Press down once to tmux, then enter.

steps.title: Split right
steps.note: Same as tmux. Each split makes a new pane.
steps.hint: Hold ctrl and tap b, let go, then % (shift+5).

steps.title: Split down
steps.note: Same as tmux.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then " (shift and the quote key).

steps.title: Move between panes
steps.note: Same arrows as tmux. One ctrl+b covers a few arrows in a row.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then any arrow key.

steps.title: Jump by number
steps.note: ctrl+b q shows a number on each pane. Type one to go there.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then q. Big numbers show. Press 2.

steps.title: Zoom in, then out
steps.note: Same as tmux.
steps.hint: ctrl+b z zooms. Do it again to unzoom.

steps.title: A new workspace
steps.note: tuios calls a tmux window a workspace. Each workspace has its own panes.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then c. The dock shows the new workspace.

steps.title: Back to the last one
steps.note: ctrl+b p goes to the previous workspace, as in tmux.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then p. Your panes wait on workspace 1.

steps.title: Copy mode, vim keys built in
steps.note: tmux used emacs keys unless you set mode-keys vi.
steps.hint: ctrl+b [ enters copy mode. / searches, enter jumps to the match, q leaves.

steps.title: Meet window mode
steps.note: New: a mode with no prefix. Single keys move panes. i types into the pane, ctrl+b esc comes back.
steps.hint: Press i. The badge says TYPING. Then ctrl+b and esc, and it says WINDOWS.

explainer.body: ctrl+b d detaches, like tmux. A daemon keeps every pane running. tuios ls lists sessions, and ctrl+b s switches between them. Put preset = "tmux" under [keybindings] to keep these keys.

tracks.title: Coming from zellij
tracks.blurb: Turn on the zellij keys, then use them: panes, tabs, floats, search.

greet: Hi. One key turns on the zellij keys. Then panes, tabs and floats.
Coming from zellij? ctrl+g and lock mode are here too.
finish: Done. Your zellij keys, locked and ready.

steps.title: Pick the zellij keys
steps.note: U opens the keybind presets. zellij is the fourth row.
steps.hint: Press shift+u. Press down three times to zellij, then enter.

steps.title: Locked, like zellij
steps.note: i starts typing. Every key now goes to the program, except ctrl+g.
steps.hint: Press i, type top and press enter. The lock in the dock means locked.

steps.title: Split right
steps.note: ctrl+g opens the menu. p is the pane menu, r splits right.
steps.hint: Hold ctrl and tap g, let go. Then p, then r.

steps.title: Split down
steps.note: Same menu, d for down.
steps.hint: ctrl+g, then p, then d.

steps.title: Move between panes
steps.note: h, j, k and l move. The menu stays open for more moves. Esc closes it.
steps.hint: ctrl+g, then p, then k to move up. Esc when you are done.

steps.title: Fullscreen, then back
steps.note: f in the pane menu, as in zellij.
steps.hint: ctrl+g, p, f fills the screen. Do it again to put it back.

steps.title: Float a pane
steps.note: e in the pane menu. Drag its title bar with the mouse to move it.
steps.hint: ctrl+g, then p, then e.

steps.title: A new tab
steps.note: A zellij tab is a tuios workspace. t is the tab menu, n makes one.
steps.hint: ctrl+g, then t, then n. The dock shows the new tab.

steps.title: Scroll and search
steps.note: s is scroll mode, here copy mode. / searches, q leaves.
steps.hint: ctrl+g, then s. Then / and tuios and enter. q leaves.

explainer.body: ctrl+g d detaches, as in zellij, and a daemon keeps it all running. ctrl+g o is the session manager. Put preset = "zellij" under [keybindings] to keep these keys.

tracks.title: Layouts
tracks.blurb: Tiles, a master and a stack, a scrolling strip, and floats.

greet: Layouts are my favourite part. My face is one.
Hi. Let us move some tiles around.
finish: You shaped every layout there is. My face approves.

steps.title: Choose where it lands
steps.note: alt and h, j, k or l picks the side. Then n.
steps.hint: Hold alt (option on a Mac), tap j, let go. Then n. The new window opens below.

terminal.hint: Hold alt, tap j, let go. Then n. On a Mac, set Option as Meta in your terminal first.

steps.title: Rotate the split
steps.note: Side by side becomes stacked, and back.
steps.hint: Press shift+r.

steps.title: Swap two windows
steps.note: shift+h, shift+j, shift+k and shift+l push the window that way.
steps.hint: shift+h swaps left. Try shift+l if nothing is to the left.

steps.title: Master and stack
steps.note: One big window on the left, the rest stacked on the right.
steps.hint: ctrl+p opens the palette. Type master-stack and press enter.

steps.title: Grow the master
steps.note: > grows it, < shrinks it.
steps.hint: > is shift and the period key.

steps.title: The scrolling strip
steps.note: Columns on an endless strip. New ones slide in, nothing shrinks.
steps.hint: ctrl+p, type scrolling, press enter.

steps.title: Widen a column
steps.note: The strip scrolls to keep it in view.
steps.hint: > widens the column, < narrows it.

steps.title: Zoom in, then out
steps.hint: z zooms the window. z again puts it back.

steps.title: Let them float, then snap
steps.note: t turns tiling off. h and l snap to a half. Floating windows can overlap, and the snapped one sits on top.
steps.hint: t floats every window. Then h snaps this one to the left half. Drag them with the mouse too.

tracks.title: Workspaces
tracks.blurb: Nine desktops in one terminal, and a side rail that shows it all.

greet: Nine workspaces, all yours. Let us visit one.
Hi. Time to spread out a little.
finish: Nine desks and you know your way around all of them.

steps.title: Visit workspace 2
steps.note: Your two windows wait on workspace 1.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then w, then 2. The dock at the top shows where you are.

steps.title: Make it yours
steps.note: Each workspace has its own windows and layout.
steps.hint: In window mode, n opens a window here.

steps.title: Jump straight back
steps.note: alt and a number skips the prefix.
steps.hint: Hold alt (option on a Mac) and press 1. ctrl+b w 1 does the same.

web.hint: Hold alt (option on a Mac) and press 1. If the browser takes it, ctrl+b w 1 does the same.

terminal.hint: Hold alt and press 1. On a Mac, set Option as Meta in your terminal. ctrl+b w 1 does the same.

steps.title: Send a window, stay here
steps.note: ctrl+alt and a number sends the window away. You stay put.
steps.hint: Hold ctrl and alt (option on a Mac), then press 2. The window leaves, and you stay on workspace 1.

terminal.hint: Hold ctrl and alt, then press 2. On a Mac, set Option as Meta in your terminal first.

steps.title: Send a window and follow
steps.note: In the workspace menu, shift and a number moves the window, and you go with it.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, w, then shift+3, which is #.

steps.title: Open the rail
steps.note: Sessions, windows, agents and files, at a glance.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then b. The rail opens on the right.

steps.title: Walk the rail
steps.note: s steps in. j and k move, enter jumps there.
steps.hint: Press s. j twice lands on the first window, the one marked w1. Enter takes you there.

steps.title: See every workspace
steps.note: A picker with a preview of each one.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then shift+w. Arrows pick one, enter goes there.

explainer.body: On your machine the rail lists every session, and sessions on your other machines too. ctrl+b S switches between them.

tracks.title: Power moves
tracks.blurb: Palette, launcher, copy mode and the scrollback browser.

greet: You know the basics. These keys save the most time.
Hi again. Palette, launcher and copy mode are next.
finish: Those are the keys that stick. Well played.

steps.title: Show your keys
steps.note: Every key you press now pops up bottom right.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then shift+d for the debug menu, then k.

steps.title: Menus inside menus
steps.note: After ctrl+b the panel lists every next key. t opens the window menu.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then t. Read the new menu, then esc.

steps.title: Run anything by name
steps.note: No key to remember. Just type.
steps.hint: ctrl+p opens the palette. Type split vertical and press enter.

steps.title: Launch a program
steps.note: ctrl+b a opens the launcher. alt+space does too.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then a. Type rain and press enter. It opens in a new window.

steps.title: Copy mode with vim keys
steps.note: hjkl, w, b, gg and G all work. / searches.
steps.hint: ctrl+b [ enters copy mode. / starts a search, type the word, enter jumps to it.

steps.title: Select and yank
steps.note: v selects, e stretches it a word, y copies. q leaves.
steps.hint: Still in copy mode: v, then e, then y. Then q to leave.

steps.title: Browse old commands
steps.note: Every command and its output, newest first.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then s. Look around, then esc closes it.

tracks.title: Pane tricks
tracks.blurb: A scratch pane, a pane in the corner, numbers, hints and the spotlight.

greet: A busy screen? These small tools keep it calm.
Hi. A scratch pane, a corner pane and the spotlight. Let us try them.
finish: Scratch, pin, numbers, hints and the spotlight. Your screen is tidy now.

steps.title: Open a scratch pane
steps.note: A pane that floats over the rest, for a quick job.
steps.hint: Hold ctrl and tap b, let go, then g.

steps.title: Hide it, keep it
steps.note: The same keys hide it. It keeps running for next time.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then g again.

steps.title: Pin a pane
steps.note: p in window mode pins the pane you are on, the rain.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then esc for window mode. Then p.

steps.title: Watch it from another pane
steps.note: The pinned pane shows in a small corner window.
steps.hint: Press tab. The rain keeps falling in the corner.

steps.title: Unpin it
steps.note: p again puts it away.
steps.hint: Press p.

steps.title: Jump by number
steps.note: Every pane gets a big number. Type one to go there.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then shift+q. Then press 1 for the rain.

steps.title: Copy what you see
steps.note: Hints put a letter on each hash, path and link. Type it to copy.
steps.hint: ctrl+b 2 goes to the git log. ctrl+b F shows the letters. Press a.

steps.title: Light up one pane
steps.note: The spotlight dims the rest of the screen. Good for a demo.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then shift+b. Look, then esc turns it off.

tracks.title: Agents
tracks.blurb: Run coding agents side by side and never miss a question.

greet: Agents live in panes here. I will show you how to keep an eye on them.
Hi. Let us start an agent and check on it from elsewhere.
finish: Now you can run agents and still get your own work done.

steps.title: Open the rail
steps.note: Every agent shows up here, with what it is doing.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then b. The rail opens on the right.

steps.title: Start an agent
steps.note: A pretend Claude Code. It runs nowhere but here.
steps.hint: Type claude and press enter. Watch the rail.

web.note: A pretend Claude Code. It never leaves this tab.

steps.title: Go do something else
steps.note: It will ask you something soon. You will know.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then w, then 2. Keep an eye on the rail and the dock.

steps.title: Jump to the question
steps.note: The rail turns orange and the dock rings. ctrl+b j takes you there.
steps.waiting: Wait for the agent to ask. The rail turns orange when it does.
steps.hint: Wait for the orange mark, then ctrl+b, then j.

steps.title: Say yes
steps.note: y approves. The mark turns green when it is done.
steps.hint: Press y, or enter on Yes.

explainer.body: On a real machine agents find each other with tuios list-agents and mail each other. ctrl+b M opens the mail between them.

steps.title: Every agent in one view
steps.note: ctrl+b i opens the agents view. The next track, The agents view, shows what it does.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then i. esc closes it.

tracks.title: The agents view
tracks.blurb: Answer, reply to and start agents from one view.

greet: Three agents are at work. Let us answer them all from one view.
Hi. One agent asks, one waits, one is done. You handle all three.
finish: You ran a whole team of agents from one view. Nice work.

steps.title: Go do something else
steps.note: Three agents work in the other panes. They keep working while you are away.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then w, then 2.

steps.title: Open the agents view
steps.note: Every agent on every workspace, grouped by what it needs from you.
steps.waiting: Wait for claude and gemini to ask. Their panes turn orange.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then i. The agents that need you are at the top.

steps.title: Read the edit first
steps.note: claude wants to edit style.css. ] goes to the next tab: the changes of its turn.
steps.hint: Press ]. [ goes back to the thread.

steps.title: Allow the edit
steps.note: Press a to ask to allow it once, then enter to send it. shift+a asks to always allow it. r asks to reject it, and shift+r to give a reason. Any key but enter drops the ask.
steps.waiting: Wait for claude to ask to edit style.css.
steps.hint: Press a, then enter. claude goes back to work.

steps.title: Peek at the question
steps.note: g goes to the top row: gemini asks which colours to use. Space reads its question.
steps.hint: Press g, then space.

steps.title: Pick an answer
steps.note: The number of an option asks to answer with it. Enter sends it, and tuios presses it in gemini's pane.
steps.hint: Press 2 for Tokyo Night, then enter.

steps.title: Reply to a finished agent
steps.note: codex is done and waits at the top. r writes to it, and enter sends.

keys.text: add a test for an empty name

steps.hint: Press g, then r. Type the reply and press enter.

steps.title: Start three attempts
steps.note: An attempt is one agent that tries the task. Several attempts of one task make a fan. n opens the New agent sheet, + adds an attempt.
steps.hint: Press n and type the task. Press shift+tab three times to reach Attempts, + twice, then enter.

steps.title: Compare, then open one
steps.note: shift+g goes to the last row, an attempt. c shows the attempts of the fan side by side. Enter opens the one under the cursor.
steps.hint: Press shift+g, then c. Wait for the attempts to finish, then press enter.

tracks.title: Automation
tracks.blurb: Tapes that drive tuios, a JSON protocol, and hooks.

greet: Tapes let tuios drive itself. Let us watch one play.
Hi. A little scripting, and then a party.
finish: You made tuios drive itself. That was fun to watch.

steps.title: Read a tape
steps.note: A tape is a script of keys and commands.
steps.hint: Type cat demo.tape and press enter.

steps.title: Press play
steps.note: Hands off. tuios types it all.
steps.hint: Type tuios tape play demo.tape and press enter. Then watch.

steps.title: Find more tapes
steps.hint: Type tuios tape list and press enter.

steps.title: Play the party tape
steps.note: Three programs, a zoom and a trip to workspace 2.
steps.hint: Type tuios tape play party.tape and press enter.

explainer.body: The daemon speaks JSON lines on its socket. Open windows, type, read panes and wait for output from any script. tuios list-verbs lists it all.
Hooks run your shell commands when a window opens, focus moves, or an agent finishes. Put them in [hooks] in your config.

tracks.title: Surfaces and diagrams
tracks.blurb: Forms, dashboards, diagrams and charts, drawn by tuios.

greet: Forms, charts and diagrams, right in your panes. Let us draw some.
Hi. Today your shell asks you a question in a real form.
finish: A form, a flowchart, a chart and a dashboard. Nice work.

steps.title: Read the markup
steps.note: TML is the markup tuios draws forms and dashboards from. A file is a tree of parts with a JSON state.
steps.hint: Type cat deploy.tml and press enter.

steps.title: Draw it as text
steps.note: tuios tml render shows the file the way a pane draws it.
steps.hint: Type tuios tml render deploy.tml and press enter.

steps.title: Open the form
steps.note: A surface is a TML file that tuios shows live, in a popup or a pane. With --wait, the command waits for your answer.
steps.hint: Type tuios tml show deploy.tml --wait and press enter.

steps.title: Move to the form
steps.note: The keyboard focus stays on your shell. ctrl+b 2 moves the focus to the form. A click works too.
steps.hint: Press ctrl+b, then 2. Or click the form.

steps.title: Deploy to production
steps.note: down and enter pick production. tab goes to Deploy. enter sends the answer to the shell.
steps.hint: Press down, enter, tab, enter. The answer prints in the shell.

steps.title: Draw the deploy flow
steps.note: tuios mermaid draws a Mermaid diagram as text that fits the pane.
steps.hint: Type tuios mermaid flow.mmd and press enter.

steps.title: Chart the sales
steps.note: tplot reads CSV and draws it in your theme's colours.
steps.hint: Type tplot sales.csv --kind bar and press enter.

steps.title: Open a dashboard pane
steps.note: A table, a chart and a diagram in one surface. --pane tiles it beside your shell.
steps.hint: Type tuios tml show status.tml --pane and press enter.

steps.title: Float the dashboard
steps.note: ctrl+b right moves to it. ctrl+b t f floats it. Press ctrl+b t f again to put it back in the tiles.
steps.hint: Press ctrl+b, then right. Then ctrl+b, t, f.

tracks.title: Files and review
tracks.blurb: Walk a project in the rail, open a file, and review its change.

greet: Hi. Let us read a project and its change, like a reviewer.
Files on the left, the diff in the middle. Let us look.
finish: You walked the files and left a note. Good review.

steps.title: Go to the project
steps.note: A small Go project. It has a change in it.
steps.hint: Type cd projects/hello and press enter.

steps.title: Open the rail
steps.note: The files section lists the folder of this pane.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then b. The rail opens on the right.

steps.title: Give the rail the keys
steps.note: ctrl+b e moves the keyboard into the rail. The same keys bring it back.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then e. The badge says SIDEBAR.

steps.title: Walk to greet.go
steps.note: j moves down and k moves up. The lit row is the cursor.
steps.hint: Press j until greet.go is lit. ctrl+b f finds a file by name.

steps.title: Open the file
steps.note: Here enter opens it in a viewer. On your machine, enter copies the path and shift+enter opens your editor.
steps.hint: With greet.go lit, press enter. q closes the viewer.

steps.title: Review the change
steps.note: ctrl+b v shows what changed in the repository of this pane.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then v. The review fills the screen.

steps.title: Jump to the next hunk
steps.note: A hunk is one block of changed lines. ] goes to the next hunk, [ to the one before. } and { go by file.
steps.hint: Press ]. The cursor moves to the next block of changes.

steps.title: Leave a note
steps.note: c writes a note on the line under the cursor. enter saves it.
steps.hint: Press c, type a few words, then press enter.

steps.title: Send your notes
steps.note: On your machine, S sends the notes to the agent in this pane. esc closes the review.
steps.hint: Press S, shift and s. The dock says what happens.

tracks.title: Ship a change
tracks.blurb: Make a worktree, change a file, review it, and open a pull request.

greet: Hi. From a new branch to a pull request, in a few steps.
Let us make a worktree and ship a small change.
finish: Branch, change, review, pull request. You shipped it.

steps.title: Make a worktree
steps.note: A worktree is a second checkout of the project on its own branch.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then U (shift and u). A dialog asks for a branch.

steps.title: Name the branch
steps.note: tuios makes the branch and the folder, and opens a pane in it.
steps.hint: Type a branch name, such as shout, and press enter.

steps.title: List the worktrees
steps.note: The new pane is in the worktree. The prompt shows its branch.
steps.hint: Type git worktree list and press enter.

steps.title: Change a file
steps.note: An agent does this part on a real machine. Here you add a line.
steps.hint: Type echo "Ship it." >> README.md and press enter.

steps.title: Review the change
steps.note: ctrl+b v shows the change against main. q closes it.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then v. Look at the change, then press q.

steps.title: See the ship steps
steps.note: tuios ship lists the steps from this worktree to a merged change.
steps.hint: Type tuios ship and press enter.

steps.title: Commit the change
steps.note: tuios ship commit commits every change on the branch.
steps.hint: Type tuios ship commit -m Docs and press enter. -m is the message.

steps.title: Open a pull request
steps.note: tuios ship pr pushes the branch and opens a pull request. In the demo, nothing leaves here.
steps.hint: Type tuios ship pr and press enter.

web.note: tuios ship pr pushes the branch and opens a pull request. In the demo, nothing leaves the tab.

tracks.title: Your keys, your way
tracks.blurb: Presets for tmux, screen and zellij, actions by name, every key.

greet: Your keys, your rules. Let us try a few presets.
Hi. Keys from tmux, screen or zellij, one menu away.
finish: Any preset, any action by name. The keys are yours now.

steps.title: Open the keybind presets
steps.note: Each preset gives you the keys of another multiplexer.
steps.hint: Press shift+u.

steps.title: Try the screen keys
steps.note: The panel says which keys your programs lose. Screen's leader is ctrl+a.
steps.hint: Press down twice to screen, then enter.

steps.title: Split the screen way
steps.note: ctrl+a, then shift+s, as in screen.
steps.hint: Hold ctrl and tap a, let go. Then shift+s.

steps.title: Hop with tab
steps.note: ctrl+a, then tab moves to the next region.
steps.hint: ctrl+a, then tab.

steps.title: Back to the tuios keys
steps.note: Every preset is a row in the palette too.
steps.hint: ctrl+p, type preset, enter. Up twice to tuios, then enter.

steps.title: Run any action by name
steps.note: In the palette, # searches every action and shows its keys.
steps.hint: ctrl+p, type #zoom, then enter on Toggle zoom.

steps.title: Every key in one list
steps.note: Search it with /. Esc closes it.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then k. Look around, then esc.

tracks.title: Look and feel
tracks.blurb: Themes, a theme editor, glyphs, borders, titles and a screen saver.

greet: Let us make tuios look like yours. Colours first.
Hi. Themes, an editor, glyphs and borders. Pick what you like.
finish: It looks like yours now. One line shares it with a friend.

steps.title: Try on a theme
steps.note: Type to filter, arrows to browse. Watch top change colour.
steps.hint: ctrl+p, type theme, enter. In the picker type nord, or browse with the arrows. Enter keeps it.

steps.title: Open the theme editor
steps.note: ctrl+f shows only the dark themes. ctrl+e edits the theme under the cursor.
steps.hint: Open the theme picker again. ctrl+f, then type nord. ctrl+e opens the editor.

steps.title: Change the accent colour
steps.note: Enter opens the colour picker. The arrows move the colour. Enter keeps it.
steps.hint: The cursor is on Accent. Press enter, then the arrow keys, then enter again.

steps.title: Drop the change
steps.note: On your machine, ctrl+s saves it as your own theme. Here, esc twice drops it.
steps.hint: Press esc. The dock asks first. Press esc again.

steps.title: Pick heavy glyphs
steps.note: ctrl+b , opens the settings. / searches them. Glyphs are the shapes of frames and marks.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then the comma key. Press / and type glyph. Enter opens the glyph picker. Type heavy and press enter.

steps.title: Draw borders with them
steps.note: Set Border style to glyphs and the frames turn heavy.
steps.hint: Esc clears the search. Press / and type border style. Left picks glyphs.

steps.title: Change the title style
steps.note: A title is a pill, a tab or plain text on the border.
steps.hint: Esc clears the search. Press / and type title style. Right picks the next style.

steps.title: Mark the rail's current row
steps.note: The rail is open on the right. Current row sets how it marks where you are.
steps.hint: Press / and type current row. Right picks the next style. Esc twice closes the page.

steps.title: Start the screen saver
steps.note: It kicks in by itself when you step away. Give it a few seconds, then any key wakes it.
steps.hint: Press shift+s. Enjoy it, then press any key.

steps.title: Keep it forever
steps.note: Your picks, saved in one file.
steps.hint: Press i to type, then cat .config/tuios/config.toml and enter.

steps.title: Share your theme
steps.note: One line holds the whole theme. Paste it in a chat.
steps.hint: Type tuios theme share nord and press enter.

tracks.title: Sessions and machines
tracks.blurb: Sessions that outlive the terminal, other machines, and your phone.

greet: Sessions keep your work when the terminal closes. Let us look around.
Hi. One rail for every session, every machine and your phone.
finish: Your work outlives the terminal now, on every machine you have.

explainer.body: A session holds your workspaces and panes. The daemon keeps it running after you close the terminal. ctrl+b d detaches, and tuios attach work brings it back.

steps.title: List your sessions
steps.note: The demo prints what a real machine shows. There, ctrl+b S switches between them.
steps.hint: Type tuios ls and press enter.

steps.title: Find sessions in the rail
steps.note: The demo has one session, local. On your machine, every session is here.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then b. The rail opens on the right.

steps.title: Go to anything
steps.note: One list of agents, sessions, workspaces and panes. Type to filter.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then shift+g. Type api and press enter.

explainer.body: tuios move-window sends a window to another session. The program in it keeps running, with its scrollback.

args: tuios note set next: run the migration

explainer.body: A return note says what comes next. Press ctrl+b, then shift+i, to write one for the session. The dock shows it when you come back.
A new tuios needs a new daemon. --dry-run shows what stops and what comes back. Each session comes back with its layout and pane history.
tuios hosts add links another machine over ssh. Its sessions and agents show in your rail, and a pane can run there.
tuios-web shows your sessions in a browser, on a phone too. Web Push tells your phone when an agent needs you.

args: tuios task add -p 'Add a jitter option, with a test' make the backoff jitter configurable

explainer.body: A task card is one piece of work in a session. An agent takes the oldest open card with tuios task claim --next. The card moves from todo to done.
